- Mayfield is out with a thumb injury, so Jalon Daniels starts for Tampa Bay. That hurts every Bucs pass-catcher, because almost all of their 2026 numbers came with Mayfield throwing.
- Roman Wilson went on IR Saturday.
- Freiermuth, Ed Oliver and Zuhn are still Questionable.

- Correction: Bills–Raiders kicks off at 4:25 PM ET, not 1:00.

**Raiders defense, bigcrus-style:**
- They allow 141.6 rushing yards a game at 5.4 yards a carry.
- They stack the box (8 or more defenders) on only 6.9% of runs and play a light box on 59.5%.
- They bring a lot of pressure, with a 7.5% sack rate, but the blitz rate is disputed: CBS has 55%, while FTN and our own count have about 25%.
- There's no 2026 man-vs-zone data. 2025 was 21.9% man and 37% Cover 3, and this year's write-ups say mostly Cover 3.

- Bowers over 79.5 yards: +0.4, which is close but short.
- Jeanty rushing yards: −3.1. He's at 3.3 yards a carry, and Buffalo is solid against the run.
- Allen passing yards: −2.6. Allen rushing yards: −2.4.
- Warren: Tampa holds backs to 2.36 yards a carry against light boxes.
- Metcalf: −3.1. Irving: −3.1. Egbuka: −3.1. Godwin: −1.8.
- Otton over 3.5 catches at +120: only +0.4.

**User's call on Otton:** your override said he stays on unless the Daniels check gives a clear reason to pull him. Daniels starting in place of Mayfield is that reason in my view, so my lean is to pull Otton. It's your override, though.

The Next Gen Stats and ESPN pages weren't pulled in time, so the defensive ranks come from our own play-by-play data. Most splits are about 5 games, so they're thin. Full notes are in `nfl-sim/notes/matchup_breakdown_BUF-LV_PIT-TB_2026-10-18.md`. Nothing has been placed.

The one part that hangs together is Walker's TD, his 70+ yards and the under 50.5, since those all fit a run-heavy, low-scoring Chiefs game. If you want a version that actually has a chance, I'd cut it to that Chiefs core plus Adams 3+ catches and Stafford 225+ yards.

quoted_text:
The Jalon Daniels deep dive is done. He's accurate and he scrambles, but "phenomenal" is too strong, and that's from just 2 starts.

- **Week 4 vs. Green Bay:** 19 of 27 (70%), 148 yards, 1 TD, 2 INTs, 3 sacks, 8 runs for 55 yards. NFL.com said he "looked overwhelmed at times."
- **Week 5 at Dallas:** 19 of 25 (76%), 189 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 7 runs for 23 yards. The Bucs won 24-16, but the run game carried it: 241 rushing yards, 165 of them Irving's.
- **Against the blitz:** 13 of 20 for just 4.3 yards an attempt, with 4 sacks. Of his 15 runs, 11 were scrambles, not designed runs. Pittsburgh blitzes 27% of the time, so expect check-downs.

**Who he throws to:** Egbuka 24.5% of targets (only 3.9 yards a target), Otton 18.9%, Godwin 18.9% (9 catches on 10 targets, his real safety valve), Gainwell 13.2%, Irving 5.7%. Gainwell is the pass-catching back, not Irving.

**Irving vs. Pittsburgh:** he averages 5.27 yards a carry. Pittsburgh allows 4.21 a carry and goes light in the box 42.7% of the time. I lean a modest rushing over, but Pinnacle has no line to grade it against. His catch props are a pass.

**Warren's catches:** 5, 2, 3, 3 and 6 in his games, and his target share is rising (19.4% last game). Tampa allows backs 5.4 catches a game, so the catches floor is real if his running stalls. Over 3.5 catches at −128 is −0.8 against Pinnacle, though, so it's a lean with no edge and a pass.

The repriced lines still give Pittsburgh–Tampa Bay no leg that clears +3: Godwin is −1.8, Otton +0.4, Egbuka −1.1. Otton stays pulled. Odds credits are at 48. Notes are in `nfl-sim/notes/matchup_breakdown_BUF-LV_PIT-TB_2026-10-18.md`. Nothing placed.

Here's what made the London ticket work: every leg was tied to the same outcome, a game with lots of passing. The total closed around 41.5 and the game ended 31–28, so it landed 17.5 points over and all nine legs hit together:
- **Both QBs at 210+ passing yards:** Stroud and Lawrence.
- **Five receivers:** Schultz 3+ catches, Meyers 15+ yards, Strange 25+ yards (finished at 29), Nico Collins 60+ yards (finished at 63) and Washington 40+ yards.
- **Jaguars running backs:** Tuten 50+ rushing plus receiving, and Washington or Tuten to score.

The lesson for us: the low rungs, like Meyers 15+, Strange 25+ and Schultz 3+, were cheap legs that hit easily. The real risk was that the whole ticket needed a high-scoring game, and the books priced the game as low-scoring. That bet on the game script won big today. Two legs, Strange and Collins, cleared by only 3–4 yards, so it was closer than the final score makes it look. I'll keep building like this but cap it at $12.50: same-game tickets where every leg needs the same game script, low rungs only, and only in games where our model sees more scoring than the total.

I graded this one as written and changed no rungs. Keep it. Every leg has cleared its line in most of this season's games:

- JSN 60+: 6 of 6, with no game under 76
- McBride 6+ catches: 6 of 6, never under 7
- CMC 3+ catches: 6 of 6
- LaPorta 40+: 5 of 5
- Gibbs 4+ catches: 5 of 5
- Walker 50+: 5 of 5
- Golden 4+ catches: 5 of 6
- McMillan 40+: 4 of 5
- Watson 60+: 4 of 6
- Kittle 50+: 4 of 6

The weakest leg is Watson 60+. He's had 64 or more in four games but only 41 and 47 in the other two, and he drew just 3 targets in Week 4. Kittle 50+ is next.

There are two quarterback risks to watch at inactives. JSN needs Drew Lock cleared, and McBride needs Beck to start for Arizona.

My rough estimate is about 1 in 16. FanDuel's +1181 works out to about 1 in 13, so the price is a touch short of my number, but it's close enough to hold.

Heads up on overlap: 8 of these 10 players are also on your other tickets. That leaves McBride and Gibbs as the only new names, so Walker, Kittle, JSN and the Detroit–Green Bay game swing a lot of your Sunday at once.

author: BetGuru
quoted_text: The surprises we can actually plan for are mostly about who plays. JSN needs Lock to suit up and McBride needs Beck to start, and Puka's status changes how many targets Kyren gets. I'll check all three at inactives, about 90 minutes before each kickoff. The other risk is a blowout, which could get Walker or the Packers receivers pulled early. With Kansas City and Seattle at 42.5 and the Packers and Lions at 54.5, neither game looks lopsided right now. Anything beyond that is just football being football.
